fixed.explanation: `filterCookies` put a dot in front of every cookie domain, so host-only cookies matched all subdomains. It also compared paths as plain string prefixes. It now matches a host-only cookie only on an exact hostname and a dotted domain on the bare domain or a suffix. Paths match only when they are equal, when the cookie path ends in '/', or when the next character of the request path is '/'. `pathMatches` appended a slash to the request path, so /foo matched a /foo/ cookie. It now uses the same RFC 6265 path-match rule.

query.intent: The cookie URL filter (filterCookies) used for listing cookies prepends a dot to every cookie domain and compares paths with plain string prefix. It should implement RFC 6265 domain-match (host-only cookies match only the exact host) and path-match (exact or slash boundary). Also the path check used when sending cookies (domainMatches/pathMatches in network cookie store) appends a slash to the request path, making /foo match /foo/.
query.symptom: Listing cookies for URLs returns host-only cookies for subdomains and for path prefixes like /apiv2, and a cookie with path /foo/ is sent to /foo.

history.analysis: filterCookies in network.ts is the buggy listing filter: it prepends a dot to every domain and uses a plain startsWith for paths. domainMatches in cookieStore.ts is correct. The pathMatches function in cookieStore.ts, which appends a slash to the request path, has not been shown yet.
